# `scripts/gadget_pkdgrav3_compare/compare_potential.py`

Source: [compare_potential.py](../../../../scripts/gadget_pkdgrav3_compare/compare_potential.py)

```text
Compare the gravitational potential of a Gadget-4 and a pkdgrav3 run started from the same ICs, particle by
particle and halo by halo, at every common output.

usage: compare_potential.py <gadget_dir> <pkd_dir> <gadget_halo_dir> <pkd_halo_dir> <out_dir> [--plot-z 3,1,0.5,0]
  gadget_dir   snapshot_<nnn>.hdf5 (with Potential), snapnames.txt         (job_gadget.pbs)
  pkd_dir      snap.<step> (HDF5) + snap.<step>.s*.pkc, snapnames.txt, p.par (pkdgrav3_pipeline job_sim.pbs, ALSO_HDF5=1)
  *_halo_dir   out_<snap>.trees (consistent-trees hlists; job_ctrees.pbs); where there is none, Rockstar's
               out_<snap>.list (all halos, no host/subhalo flag) is used instead
Output in out_dir: particles.csv (one row per output), halos.csv (one row per matched halo and output),
summary.json, snap_<nnn>.npz (particle and halo arrays of the outputs closest to --plot-z, for plot_compare.py).

Conventions (all potentials in peculiar, physical (km/s)^2):
  Gadget-4: Potential attribute scaling a^-1 (snap_io.cc): phi = Potential / a. Self-interaction removed
            (gravity.cc), zero point of the periodic TreePM potential = volume mean 0.
  pkdgrav3: phi = Potential_code * U^2 / a, U = 100 L / sqrt(8 pi / 3) km/s (G = 1, rho_crit = 3/(8 pi), L = 1);
            the same as its .pkc potential (checked here). It keeps each particle's softened self-interaction,
            -(105/64) m / eps (gravity/pp.h at r = 0), a constant for equal masses: phi_pkd_corr = phi - that.
  The two codes can still differ by a constant per snapshot (zero point of the periodic potential, e.g. how a
  particle's own periodic images are counted: on a uniform lattice that is the Madelung term 2.837 m/d). It changes
  no force. particles.csv reports it (offset_median of phi_pkd_corr - phi_gadget); the halo values and snap_*.npz use
  pkdgrav3 potentials aligned by it (phi_pkd_corr - offset_median).
  Particles are matched by ID: Gadget ID - 1 = pkdgrav3 iOrder (gadget4_ic_to_gadget2.py).
  Velocities, peculiar km/s: Gadget-4 Velocities * sqrt(a) (a_scaling 0.5); pkdgrav3 Velocities * U * a.
  particles.csv: dr_* = |x_pkd - x_gadget| (Mpc/h), dv_* = |v_pkd - v_gadget| (km/s), v_corr (all components),
  v_slope (least squares v_pkd = s v_gadget), v_rms_* = sqrt(<|v|^2>).
  Independent reference: periodic FFT Poisson solution of each snapshot's own particles (CIC on --grid^3,
  deconvolved), lap phi = 1.5 Om H0^2 delta / a, mean 0, interpolated (CIC) to the particles.
Halos: host halos (pid = -1) of each code's out_<snap>.trees with >= --min-np particles within Rvir. For each halo,
  from its own snapshot: particles within Rvir of the centre -> phi_min, <phi>, and <phi> of the 10% most bound.
  Gadget halos are matched to pkdgrav3 halos by mutual nearest centre within 0.5 Rvir_gadget and |log10 M ratio|
  < 0.3. Lagrangian check: the pkdgrav3 potential of the Gadget halo's member particles (same IDs).
```

## Contents

- [`wrap`](#wrap) - Wrap positions into [0, L) (also maps values that round to L onto 0, as cKDTree requires).
- [`read_par`](#read_par) - The few scalar values of pkdgrav3's p.par that are needed (dSoft may be an expression).
- [`read_gadget`](#read_gadget) - Read a Gadget-4 HDF5 snapshot (dark matter only), ordered by particle ID.
- [`read_pkd`](#read_pkd) - Read a pkdgrav3 HDF5 snapshot (rows ordered by iOrder) in the box `L` (Mpc/h).
- [`pkc_check`](#pkc_check) - max |phi\_pkc - phi\_hdf5| (km/s)^2 and the pkc potential step; None if pkcreader is not importable.
- [`cic_weights`](#cic_weights) - Cloud-in-cell cell index and fractional offset of each position on an `n`^3 grid of box `L`.
- [`fft_potential`](#fft_potential) - Peculiar potential (km/s)^2 at the particles from a CIC density on n^3 (deconvolved twice: assignment and interpolation), lap phi = 1.5 Om H0^2 delta / a, k = 0 mode zero.
- [`fit`](#fit) - slope, offset, correlation of y vs x, and rms of y - (slope x + offset).
- [`read_hlist`](#read_hlist) - Read a consistent-trees hlist (or Rockstar list) into a dict of column arrays, names without the `(n)` suffix; an empty file gives empty columns.
- [`halo_file`](#halo_file) - consistent-trees catalogue out\_&lt;i&gt;.trees, else Rockstar's out\_&lt;i&gt;.list (e.g. too few halos for ctrees).
- [`halo_props`](#halo_props) - Per host halo: particles within Rvir of the centre in this snapshot.
- [`match`](#match) - Mutual nearest centres within 0.5 Rvir\_gadget and |log10 Mg/Mp| &lt; 0.3 -&gt; list of (ig, ip, distance).
- [`main`](#main) - Command line: compare the particle potentials of a Gadget-4 and a pkdgrav3 run from the same ICs (particle by particle, against a grid Poisson solution, and around matched halos); writes CSV tables and plots to `out_dir`.

## wrap

```python
wrap(x, L)
```

Wrap positions into [0, L) (also maps values that round to L onto 0, as cKDTree requires).

## read_par

```python
read_par(path)
```

The few scalar values of pkdgrav3's p.par that are needed (dSoft may be an expression).

## read_gadget

```python
read_gadget(path)
```

Read a Gadget-4 HDF5 snapshot (dark matter only), ordered by particle ID.

Returns `(a, L, pos, phi, vel)`: positions in Mpc/h, peculiar potential phi = Potential / a in (km/s)^2 and
peculiar velocities in km/s (Velocities \* sqrt(a)).

## read_pkd

```python
read_pkd(path, L)
```

Read a pkdgrav3 HDF5 snapshot (rows ordered by iOrder) in the box `L` (Mpc/h).

Returns `(a, pos, phi, U, vel)`: positions in [0, L), phi = Potential U^2 / a in (km/s)^2, the velocity
unit U = H0 L / sqrt(8 pi / 3) and peculiar velocities v U a in km/s.

## pkc_check

```python
pkc_check(prefix, phi_hdf5)
```

max |phi\_pkc - phi\_hdf5| (km/s)^2 and the pkc potential step; None if pkcreader is not importable.

## cic_weights

```python
cic_weights(pos, n, L)
```

Cloud-in-cell cell index and fractional offset of each position on an `n`^3 grid of box `L`.

## fft_potential

```python
fft_potential(pos, n, L, a, Om)
```

Peculiar potential (km/s)^2 at the particles from a CIC density on n^3 (deconvolved twice: assignment and
interpolation), lap phi = 1.5 Om H0^2 delta / a, k = 0 mode zero.

## fit

```python
fit(x, y)
```

slope, offset, correlation of y vs x, and rms of y - (slope x + offset).

## read_hlist

```python
read_hlist(path)
```

Read a consistent-trees hlist (or Rockstar list) into a dict of column arrays, names without the
`(n)` suffix; an empty file gives empty columns.

## halo_file

```python
halo_file(d, i)
```

consistent-trees catalogue out\_&lt;i&gt;.trees, else Rockstar's out\_&lt;i&gt;.list (e.g. too few halos for ctrees).

## halo_props

```python
halo_props(h, pos, phi, tree, L, mp, min_np)
```

Per host halo: particles within Rvir of the centre in this snapshot.

## match

```python
match(hg, hp, L)
```

Mutual nearest centres within 0.5 Rvir\_gadget and |log10 Mg/Mp| &lt; 0.3 -&gt; list of (ig, ip, distance).

## main

```python
main()
```

Command line: compare the particle potentials of a Gadget-4 and a pkdgrav3 run from the same ICs
(particle by particle, against a grid Poisson solution, and around matched halos); writes CSV tables and
plots to `out_dir`.
